## Project Format

Each project is designed for a team of **two or three students** and culminates in a **10–12 minute presentation** supported by a concise analyst-style exhibit package. Coding is optional; a spreadsheet is sufficient. Teams must state assumptions and conventions, cite all external sources, distinguish observed data from estimates, and explain limitations.

Unless a project states otherwise, submit presentation slides in PDF, a reproducible exhibit package, and a one-page source-and-assumptions note. Every project is graded using a **100-point rubric** shown with the project.

## Model submission

Before starting, review the [Sample Project and Complete Model Deliverable](sample-project.qmd). It shows the expected depth of sourcing, calculations, exhibits, financial judgment, limitations, and 10–12 minute presentation structure. The sample is a template for quality and organization, not a required topic.

::: {.callout-note}
## Professional standard
Emphasize financial reasoning, tradeoffs, and a defensible recommendation. Use manageable samples and instructor-provided dated snapshots when historical market data are unavailable.
:::
